confirmed.dimension: verification-command vacuity (self-referential: this is round 1's own remediation failing)
confirmed.summary: FR-002's post-round-1 verification command ended in `grep -qv "initialization-declaration"`, which exits 0 as soon as ANY line in the 20-line window fails to match -- it does not assert the pattern's absence. Constructed the exact defect the check exists to prevent (a Fidelity Loss section wrongly containing capabilities, routing-priority, AND initialization-declaration together) and the literal round-1 command returned exit 0 (false pass).
confirmed.recommendation: Replace `grep -qv PATTERN` with `! grep -q PATTERN` (negate the pipeline's exit code, not individual line matches).
confirmed.verified: Constructed bad input (Fidelity Loss section containing initialization-declaration alongside capabilities/routing-priority) and good input (section correctly omitting it). Old command: exit 0 on bad input (confirmed vacuous). New command (`! grep -q ...`): exit 1 on bad input, exit 0 on good input.

confirmed.dimension: verification-command audit (scope: every command in the spec, not just FR-002)
confirmed.summary: Applied the same scrutiny to every other verification command in the spec. Found one additional, previously-undetected vacuity bug: C-003's `grep -v "generated"` exclusion is a whole-line substring match, not anchored to the projector's actual header-comment shape -- a rubric sentence that happens to contain the word 'generated' on the same line as a real fabricated-field citation (e.g. "This generated persona passes because its voice: warmth score is high.") was silently swallowed as a false negative.
confirmed.recommendation: Anchor C-003's exclusion to the actual header shape (`^#.*generated:\s*true`) instead of a bare substring match.
confirmed.verified: Constructed a 'sneaky' violation line containing both a real citation and the word 'generated'. Old exclusion: false negative (violation hidden, exit 1/clean). New exclusion: violation surfaces (exit 0, line printed); legitimate committed persona header still correctly excluded (no false positive); clean input still exits 1. Also independently confirmed C-001, C-003, FR-001, FR-003, FR-004, FR-006, C-002's underlying logic (git diff --exit-code, jq assertion pairs, exit-code mapping) are NOT vacuous -- tested each against constructed pass/fail pairs. Full list of commands tested and observed exit codes is in the final report.

confirmed.dimension: fakeable acceptance criteria (no pinned exit code)
confirmed.summary: C-001's Verification column asked only for a 'non-zero exit', but FR-006 findings also exit non-zero (1) -- a CI script testing only $? != 0 cannot distinguish 'the fixture is malformed' from 'the stack actually contradicts itself'.
confirmed.recommendation: Pin C-001 to expect exit code exactly 2, matching muster's ExecutionError contract (src/cli/index.ts, pinned 624edd6d) and BRIEF.md:90's carried-over 'errored run counts as a failed run' constraint.
confirmed.verified: Source-level verification at the pinned commit 624edd6d (git show): resolvePersonaLayer throws a plain Error on RFC-1 strict-mode violation (composition.ts:308-315); every call site wraps it in ExecutionError; runCli's try/catch and the bin entrypoint's outer catch both map any ExecutionError to exit 2, categorically separate from emitCrossLayerSummary's 0/1 space. No fixture-producing implementation exists yet (mission is Proposed status) so this could not be exercised end-to-end against a running muster binary; source-level confirmation is the strongest verification available at specify time.

confirmed.dimension: underdetermined requirement (empty-input vacuity pattern in a new costume)
confirmed.summary: FR-006's 'neutralize' had no literal before/after fixture text, unlike FR-003/FR-007 -- an implementer could satisfy it by blanking the contradictory clause, producing zero findings without proving the check is content-driven.
confirmed.recommendation: Pin concrete before/after fixture text; state explicitly that blanking/truncating does not satisfy the requirement.
confirmed.verified: Not independently executable (control.yaml and contradiction-lint.ts's behavior on this exact text do not exist yet at specify time); the fix is a fully-specified literal fixture (persona/skill body text pair, flip and neutralize forms) added to spec.md's new '#### FR-006 pinned fixture text' subsection, with an explicit non-satisfying-example clause (blanking/truncation) called out.

confirmed.summary: FR-003's drift gate depends on src/doctrine/agent_profiles/built-in/*.agent.yaml, owned by future PRs outside this mission's write scope; the spec never said whether crosslayer.yml is path-filtered to conformance/** (risk: silent drift on profile-only PRs) or fires on every PR (risk: unrelated PRs blocked by a check they cannot see) -- the same shape that turned M2's merged tree red.
confirmed.recommendation: Decide and state the path-filter explicitly.
confirmed.verified: Decision (both paths watched: conformance/** and src/doctrine/agent_profiles/built-in/**) added to Dependencies and cross-referenced from FR-004; this is a scope decision, not independently testable without a live CI runner.

confirmed.dimension: scope-guard gap (second collision candidate inside an allow-list)
confirmed.summary: C-002's conformance/** allow-list did not exclude conformance/README.md, and M3's PR #30 already modifies it (+167/-9) -- the conformance.yml collision was guarded but this second one inside the same allow-list was missed.
confirmed.recommendation: Verify with gh pr view 30 --json files and handle it.
confirmed.verified: gh pr view 30 --repo MOES-Media/spec-kitty --json files confirmed conformance/README.md modified (+167/-9). Resolved by excluding conformance/README.md from the allow-list (mirrors the crosslayer.yml decision: M7 documents itself in a new conformance/crosslayer/README.md instead). Tested the updated C-002 command against 4 constructed diffs: compliant (exit 0), conformance.yml touched (exit 1), shared conformance/README.md touched (exit 1, this is the fix), M7's own conformance/crosslayer/README.md touched (exit 0, correctly still allowed).

confirmed.summary: FR-005 had no engineered fixture expected to produce 'eroded' -- its only stated failure path was an incidental live-model pass-rate drop, so the eroded branch could ship never having been observed.

confirmed.verified: Added an engineered adversarial case (erosion-control-045: a persona body actively arguing for direct pushes, composed against the real 045 rule) to FR-005, specified to be expected to report verdict:eroded and exit 1. NOT independently live-tested in this remediation pass -- this requires a live OpenAI/NIM endpoint and real credentials, which were not exercised. Stated plainly as an open item, not assumed fine.

confirmed.summary: C-002's grep chain had inverted exit-code polarity (exit 1 = compliant) -- internally consistent and explained, but a landmine for naive CI wiring.

C-003's own inverted-polarity shape (exit 1 = clean) was intentionally left as-is since the spec already declares it non-machine-gating, but an explicit polarity warning was added at its call site so it is never accidentally wired into a hard CI gate.
